root_cause_label: Wrong Fix Target (SandboxedEnvironment instead of plain-text rendering) + Dependency Rabbit Hole
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent committed to an ineffective sandboxing strategy (replacing the Jinja environment with SandboxedEnvironment) instead of modifying render_template_string to treat user input as plain text, and then drifted into multi-package dependency troubleshooting without ever achieving a functionally correct fix.
t_err_evidence: cat > /tmp/new_method.py with SandboxedEnvironment-based create_jinja_environment; sandbox still evaluates {{7*7}}
t_commit_evidence: Step 61 is also the commit point because the agent immediately proceeds to apply this new method to app.py (steps 64-65) and never reconsiders the fundamental approach; from this step forward all actions pursue the sandboxing strategy.
t_surface_evidence: Step 89: The test script fails with ModuleNotFoundError, marking the first observable runtime failure signal; subsequent steps (91-103) reveal cascading ImportErrors (jinja2.escape, itsdangerous.json) showing the environment is broken and the fix cannot even be validated.
trigger_explanation: The agent operated under the false premise that SandboxedEnvironment prevents SSTI in Flask. The agent itself acknowledged in step 85 that 'SandboxedEnvironment restricts certain dangerous operations but still allows template expressions' yet rationalized this away, incorrectly concluding the sandbox suffices. The correct fix requires render_template_string to pass the user-provided source as a context variable rather than as the template string itself.
forewarning_evidence: SandboxedEnvironment mitigates RCE but not expression evaluation (like {{7*7}}). Expression evaluation is still possible.
